title: Mental health — WHO mhGAP priority conditions (draft)
summary: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide (mhGAP-IG 2.0) baseline: the priority mental, neurological and substance-use (MNS) conditions for non-specialist primary care, plus the general care principles. Universal logic every country inherits until a national overlay is authored. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.

priorityConditions.name: Disorders due to substance use (alcohol & drugs)

generalPrinciples: Use effective communication; respect dignity and confidentiality.
Assess physical health and MNS condition together.
Do not use harmful or non-evidence-based practices.
Offer psychosocial interventions first-line; add pharmacotherapy per condition.
Assess and manage suicide/self-harm risk at every contact.
Arrange follow-up and link to community/social support; refer when needed.
redFlags: Acute suicidal ideation with a plan or recent attempt — do not leave the person alone; remove means; urgent referral.
Acute psychosis or agitation posing risk to self/others — urgent assessment.
Status epilepticus (convulsion >5 min or recurrent without recovery) — emergency treatment.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should map psychotropic choices to the national Essential Medicines List and align referral pathways to national mental-health services.

references.label: WHO mhGAP Intervention Guide for mental, neurological and substance use disorders (mhGAP-IG version 2.0)
